s: The setting up of the Planning Commission was in line with which Article of the Constitution?
x: The Planning Commission was established in line with the objectives reflected in Article 39 of the Directive Principles.

s: When was the Planning Commission set up?
x: It was set up on 15 March 1950 by a Cabinet resolution and began work on 28 March 1950.

s: How was the Planning Commission set up?
x: It was set up by a Cabinet (executive) resolution, so it was non-constitutional and non-statutory.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Planning Commission:
1. It was a non-statutory, advisory body.
2. Its last Five Year Plan was the Eleventh.
3. It was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Commission was non-statutory and advisory and gave way to NITI Aayog in 2015; its last Plan was the Twelfth (2012-17).

s: What was the National Planning Council set up in 1965?
o: An expert advisory body attached to the Planning Commission
A body of State Chief Ministers
x: The National Planning Council of 1965 was an expert advisory body attached to the Planning Commission.

s: On which system was the Planning Commission broadly modelled?
x: The Planning Commission was modelled on the Soviet Gosplan planning organisation.

s: On which date was the Planning Commission replaced by NITI Aayog?
x: NITI Aayog succeeded the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

s: Which body was set up after Independence to prepare a common plan for the country?
x: The Planning Commission (15 March 1950) was the body set up after Independence for a common plan.

s: By what means was the National Development Council set up in August 1952?
o: A resolution of the Supreme Court
x: The National Development Council was established in August 1952 through an executive resolution.

s: What is the status of the National Development Council?
x: The NDC is neither constitutional nor statutory, works in an advisory capacity, and its recommendations are not binding.

s: At least how often was the National Development Council expected to meet?
x: The NDC was meant to meet at least twice a year; it approved the draft Five-Year Plans.

s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that the National Development Council should be given constitutional status under
o: Article 263 and renamed the National Economic and Development Council
Article 243ZD and renamed the District Development Council
Article 280 and renamed the Finance Council
Article 356 and renamed the Union Development Council
x: The Sarkaria Commission recommended constitutional status for the Council under Article 263 and suggested the name National Economic and Development Council.

s: Which statement regarding the National Development Council is correct after the creation of NITI Aayog?
o: It was converted into a statutory tribunal.
It was abolished by a constitutional amendment on 1 January 2015.
It became the fund-allocating arm of NITI Aayog.
x: A formal resolution abolishing the National Development Council remains pending; replacement of the Planning Commission did not itself complete that formal abolition.

s: With reference to the National Development Council (NDC), which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Secretary — Secretary of the Planning Commission
Chairman — Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission
x: The Prime Minister chaired the NDC and the Secretary of the Planning Commission acted as its Secretary; Chief Ministers of all states were members. The President is not a member, the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission was not its chairman, and the Cabinet Secretary was not its secretary.

s: Who among the following is NOT a member of the National Development Council?
x: The Chairman of the Finance Commission is not a member of the National Development Council. Its membership included the Prime Minister, Union Cabinet Ministers, State Chief Ministers, Union Territory administrators and Planning Commission members.

s: To which body has the role of the now-inactive National Development Council passed?
x: The NDC is inactive; its role passed to NITI Aayog's Governing Council, with formal abolition pending.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Development Council:
1. It prescribed guidelines for the national plan, including assessment of resources.
2. Its advice was binding on the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Prescribing plan guidelines including resource assessment was an NDC function, but its advice was not binding.

s: Who was the Secretary of the National Development Council?
x: The Secretary of the Planning Commission served as the NDC's Secretary.

s: Which of the following is a function of the National Development Council?
o: To audit the accounts of the Union and the States
To decide the share of States in central taxes
To ensure balanced development of all regions of the country
To estimate poverty at the national and state level
x: The NDC was set up to secure States' cooperation, mobilise resources, promote common economic policies and ensure balanced development of all regions.

s: On whose recommendation was the National Development Council set up in 1952?
o: The draft outline of the First Five Year Plan
x: The NDC was set up in August 1952 by an executive resolution, on the recommendation of the draft outline of the First Plan.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Development Council:
1. It was set up in 1950, along with the Planning Commission.
2. It was an extra-constitutional apex body that finally approved the Five Year Plans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Planning Commission came in 1950 but the NDC only in 1952, so 1 is wrong; 2 is correct.

s: When was the National Development Council set up?
x: The NDC came on 6 August 1952, not 1950 with the Planning Commission.

s: Who is regarded as the “Father of Indian Planning” and authored *Planned Economy for India* in 1934?
x: M. Visvesvaraya authored *Planned Economy for India* in 1934 and is regarded as the Father of Indian Planning.

s: Who chaired the Congress National Planning Committee, which was initiated by Subhas Chandra Bose?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the committee; its final report came in 1949.

s: The Bombay Plan of 1944 was prepared by
o: members of the National Planning Committee and advocated agricultural collectivisation
eight industrialists and advocated state-led industrialisation with protection
village-level workers and advocated complete decentralisation
Marxist economists and focused exclusively on basic necessities
x: The Bombay Plan was prepared by eight industrialists, including J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla and Kasturbhai Lalbhai, and sought state-led industrialisation and protection.

s: Which of the following plans was based on the idea of decentralised and self-contained villages?
x: The Gandhian Plan, prepared by Shriman Narayan Agarwal in 1944, emphasised decentralised and self-contained villages.

s: What did the Karachi Resolution of 1931 advocate in the economic sphere?
o: Free trade with no state ownership
Economic freedom and state ownership of key industries
x: The 1931 Karachi Resolution supported economic freedom and state ownership of key industries.

s: Who among the following was NOT a signatory to the Bombay Plan?
x: The Bombay Plan included industrialists and economists such as J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla and John Mathai. M.N. Roy was associated with the People's Plan, not the Bombay Plan.

s: In which year did the Congress National Planning Committee of 1938 submit its final report?
x: The NPC, chaired by Nehru, gave its final report in 1949.

s: Who prepared the People's Plan?
x: M.N. Roy prepared the People's Plan; he was not a Bombay Plan signatory.

s: Who headed the Planning and Development Department set up in 1944?
x: The Planning and Development Department was set up in 1944 under Ardeshir Dalal and abolished in 1946.

s: Which group among the following supported planning in pre-independence India and prepared the Bombay Plan?
x: The Bombay Plan of 1944 was prepared by eight industrialists; industrialists and socialists were the main supporters of planning.

s: What was the aim of the ten-year plan in M. Visvesvaraya's 'Planned Economy for India' (1934)?
o: To treble the national income in 15 years
x: Visvesvaraya's 1934 plan proposed a ten-year plan to double national income by shifting labour to industry.

s: With which session of the Indian National Congress is the setting up of the National Planning Committee (1938) by Subhas Chandra Bose associated?
x: Subhas Chandra Bose, as Congress President at Haripura (1938), initiated the National Planning Committee; Nehru chaired it.

s: Who prepared the Gandhian Plan of 1944?
x: The Gandhian Plan (1944), based on decentralised self-contained villages, was prepared by Shriman Narayan Agarwal.

s: Under whom was the Economic Programme Committee of 1947 set up?
x: The Economic Programme Committee of 1947 worked under Jawaharlal Nehru.

s: Who headed the Advisory Planning Board that recommended the setting up of the Planning Commission in 1950?
x: The Advisory Planning Board of 1946, headed by K.C. Neogi, recommended the establishment of the Planning Commission.

s: Who among the following was NOT a signatory to the Bombay Plan?
x: M.N. Roy prepared the People's Plan and was not a Bombay Plan signatory.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Gandhian Plan was by Shriman Narayan Agarwal; the People's Plan by M.N. Roy and Sarvodaya by J.P. Narayan.

s: Who chaired the Congress National Planning Committee (1938)?
x: Bose initiated the NPC, but Nehru chaired it.

s: Who prepared the Sarvodaya Plan of 1950?
x: The Sarvodaya Plan (1950) was prepared by Jayaprakash Narayan, not by Vinoba Bhave himself.

s: Which plan of 1945, prepared by M.N. Roy of the Indian Federation of Labour, gave priority to agriculture?
x: M.N. Roy's People's Plan (1945) was a ten-year plan that gave priority to agriculture.

s: Which plan of 1934 aimed to double India's national income in ten years?
x: M. Visvesvaraya's 'Planned Economy for India' (1934) proposed doubling national income in ten years.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Finance Commission constituted?
x: The Finance Commission is under Article 280; the Planning Commission (1950) and NITI Aayog (2015) were set up by Cabinet resolutions.

s: Who is the Chairman of a State Planning Board?
x: The Chief Minister chairs the State Planning Board and submitted the State draft plan to the Planning Commission.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Finance Commission – Tax devolution and grants
Finance Commission – Planning and resource allocation
Planning Commission – Tax devolution and grants
National Development Council – Tax devolution and grants
x: The Finance Commission handles tax sharing and grants; the Planning Commission handled planning and resource allocation.

s: Which body assessed resources and prepared the draft Five Year Plan?
x: The Planning Commission assessed resources and drafted the plan; the NDC approved it.

s: Under the old planning framework, which body made the budgetary allocation for plan spending?
x: The Finance Ministry made budgetary allocation for plan spending.

s: Besides the Chairman and Vice-Chairman, how many members does a State Planning Board have?
x: A State Planning Board has the CM as Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and 6-9 members.

s: To which body did the Chief Minister send the draft plan of a State for approval?
x: The State Planning Board drafted the state plan and the Chief Minister sent it to the Planning Commission.

s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman; Nehru, as PM, was the first Chairman.

s:
Consider the following pairs about the Planning Commission:
1. First Deputy Chairman – Gulzarilal Nanda
2. Last Deputy Chairman – M.S. Ahluwalia
3. Last Five-Year Plan – Eleventh Plan
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first and M.S. Ahluwalia the last Deputy Chairman; the last Plan was the Twelfth (2012-17), not the Eleventh.

s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission; M.S. Ahluwalia was the last.

s: What rank did the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission hold?
o: Secretary to the Government of India
x: The Deputy Chairman was the de facto head, with Cabinet-minister rank, attending Cabinet meetings without a vote.

s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the Planning Commission's regular composition?
o: A Member-Secretary drawn from the senior IAS
The Governors of all States as members
The Finance Minister as an ex officio member
x: States and Governors were not represented in the composition of the Planning Commission. It included the Prime Minister, Finance and Planning Ministers ex officio, expert members and a Member-Secretary.

s: Who was the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission from June 1991 to May 1996?
x: Pranab Mukherjee was Deputy Chairman from June 1991 to May 1996.

s: Who among the following served as Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission from January 1985 to August 1987?
x: Manmohan Singh was Deputy Chairman from January 1985 to August 1987; P. Chidambaram never held the post.

s: Which of the following bodies is statutory?
x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies. The National Development Council and the Planning Commission were neither constitutional nor statutory, being set up by executive resolutions, and NITI Aayog's Governing Council is likewise not statutory.

s: In which List and Entry of the Constitution of India is 'Economic and social planning' included?
x: Economic and social planning is placed in the Concurrent List under Entry 20 of List III.

s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government?
x: Article 40 deals with village panchayats; Article 39 is the source of plan objectives.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about planning bodies and the Constitution?
o: The Planning Commission is not mentioned in the Constitution
The NITI Governing Council is statutory
x: Zonal Councils are statutory, but the NDC, Planning Commission and NITI Governing Council are not.

s: Which Entry of the Concurrent List deals with 'Economic and social planning'?
x: Economic and social planning is Entry 20 of List III (Concurrent List), Seventh Schedule.

s: In which Plan did Andhra Pradesh first introduce district-level decentralised planning, and with what allocation?
o: Seventh Plan, with Rs 1 crore for each of 26 districts
Eighth Plan, with Rs 2 crore for each of 23 districts
Sixth Plan, with Rs 1 crore for each of 23 districts
Fifth Plan, with Rs 50 lakh for each of 13 districts
x: Andhra Pradesh introduced district-level decentralised planning during the Sixth Plan (1980–85), allocating Rs 1 crore to each of its 23 districts and setting up District Planning Councils.

s: During which Plan was the Andhra Pradesh State Planning Commission set up?
x: The AP State Planning Commission was set up during the Fifth Plan (1974-79).

s: Under which Article are Metropolitan Planning Committees provided for?
x: MPCs are under Article 243ZE; DPCs are under Article 243ZD.

s: The Thungon sub-committee (1988) made which body the pivot of planning?
x: The Thungon sub-committee made the Zila Parishad, not the Gram Sabha, the pivot of planning.

s: Who forwards the draft district plan consolidated by the District Planning Committee to the State Government?
o: Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad
x: The DPC chairperson forwards the draft district plan, consolidated from Panchayat and Municipal plans, to the State Government.

s: What share of the members of a Metropolitan Planning Committee is elected?
x: Two-thirds of MPC members are elected; four-fifths is the figure for a District Planning Committee.

s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, inserted which Part into the Constitution of India?
x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, dealing with municipalities, into the Constitution.

s: Under which Article is the District Planning Committee provided for?
x: DPCs are under Article 243ZD in Part IXA; 243ZE is for Metropolitan Planning Committees.

s: For metropolitan areas of what population is a Metropolitan Planning Committee set up?
x: MPCs are for metropolitan areas of 10 lakh or more.

s: What share of the members of a District Planning Committee must be elected by and from the elected members of the district panchayat and municipalities?
x: Under Article 243ZD, at least four-fifths of a DPC's members are elected from the elected members of the district panchayat and municipalities.

s: Which committee recommended in 1957 that planning be entrusted to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended entrusting planning to PRIs; it was accepted in January 1958.

s: In India's multi-level planning, which is the planning body at the district level?
x: Planning runs through NITI Aayog (Centre), Planning Boards (States), DPCs (districts) and GPDPs at the village level.

s: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments are significant in the context of planning because they:
o: Made NITI Aayog a constitutional body
Restored the role of local bodies in development planning
x: The 73rd and 74th Amendments strengthened and restored the role of rural and urban local bodies in local development planning.

s: How many districts does the Amaravati Economic Region of Andhra Pradesh comprise?
x: The Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati Economic Regions have 10, 9 and 10 districts respectively.

s: Which of the following groups consisted of programmes that operated outside the panchayats?
o: GPDP, DPC, NITI Aayog and SFDA
DPAP, NDC, IADP and Planning Boards
x: The Small Farmers Development Agency (SFDA), Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP), Integrated Tribal Development Programme (ITDP) and Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) operated outside the panchayat framework.

s: Which committee of 1961 flagged growing centralisation in planning?
x: The JP Narayan Committee (1961) flagged growing centralisation.

s: In which year was Kerala's People's Plan Campaign for decentralised planning launched?
x: Kerala's People's Plan Campaign was launched on 17 August 1996, giving 35-40% of plan outlay to local bodies.

s: Which economic region of Andhra Pradesh is being planned with the assistance of NITI Aayog?
x: The Visakhapatnam Economic Region (10 districts) is NITI-assisted and was launched on 13 November 2025.

s: What does NITI Aayog's State Support Mission help States to set up?
x: The State Support Mission helps States set up State Institutions for Transformation.

s: How many districts does the Visakhapatnam Economic Region of Andhra Pradesh cover?
x: The Visakhapatnam and Tirupati Economic Regions have 10 districts each; Amaravati has 9.

s: Which one of the following statements about NITI Aayog is correct?
o: It performs a think-tank role and promotes bottom-up and cooperative-federal planning.
It is a constitutional body responsible for approving Five-Year Plans.
It functions primarily as a fund allocator to the States.
It replaced Panchayati Raj Institutions in district planning.
x: NITI Aayog is described as a think tank that promotes bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism; it is not primarily a fund allocator.

s: The Planning Commission was described as a “super cabinet”, “economic cabinet”, “parallel cabinet” and “the fifth wheel of the coach” mainly because it was criticised for
o: centralising decision-making and eroding State autonomy
transferring all financial powers to local bodies
restricting planning to the private sector
x: These epithets reflected criticism that the Planning Commission centralised decisions and weakened the autonomy of the States.

s: Who admitted in 1958 that the Planning Commission had become a kind of 'super-cabinet'?
x: Nehru admitted in 1958 that the Commission had come to be seen as a 'super-cabinet'.

s: Which body's 'common plan' idea bred lasting Centre-State tension?
x: The Advisory Planning Board's 'common plan' idea bred lasting Centre-State tension.

s: Which of the following distinguishes NITI Aayog from the former Planning Commission?
o: NITI Aayog is a constitutional body whereas the Planning Commission was statutory.
NITI Aayog is a fund allocator and the Planning Commission was only a think tank.
NITI Aayog prepares the Union Budget in place of the Finance Ministry.
NITI Aayog emphasises bottom-up and cooperative federalism and functions as a think tank rather than a fund allocator.
x: NITI Aayog emphasises bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism and functions primarily as a think tank, not as a fund allocator.

s: NITI Aayog has no financial powers. With which of the following is it associated?
x: NITI Aayog has no financial powers and marks a shift to cooperative and competitive federalism.

s: Under a rolling plan, the plan is:
o: Revised once at the end of five years
Kept fixed until the perspective plan ends
Revised every year and extended by one year
Revised every two years and extended by two years
x: A rolling plan is revised annually and extended forward by one year, giving flexibility in targets.

s: What was a major criticism of the rolling plan?
o: Yearly revision weakened commitment to targets
x: Frequent yearly revision was criticised because it weakened commitment to the originally stated targets.

s:
Consider the following statements about the rolling plan:
1. It was introduced by the Janata Party government.
2. It was in force from April 1978 to March 1980.
3. It was suggested by P.C. Mahalanobis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Janata government ran the rolling plan from April 1978 to March 1980; it was suggested by Gunnar Myrdal, not Mahalanobis.

s: Who suggested the concept of the rolling plan for developing countries?
x: Gunnar Myrdal suggested the rolling plan for backward countries; the Janata government adopted it in 1978.

s: In which book did Gunnar Myrdal put forward the idea of the rolling plan?
o: Indian Economic Planning in its Broader Setting
x: Myrdal suggested the rolling plan in 'Indian Economic Planning in its Broader Setting'.

s: Which Plan of the Janata government came to be known as the 'rolling plan'?
x: The Janata government's draft Sixth Plan (1978-83) was the rolling plan, its novel idea.

s: Which Five Year Plan did the Janata Party government end a year early before adopting the Rolling Plan?
x: The Janata government ended the Fifth Plan (1974-79) a year early in 1978 and adopted the Rolling Plan.

s: From which date did the Congress government's Sixth Five Year Plan begin after the Rolling Plan ended?
x: After the Janata government fell and the 1979-80 annual plan, the Congress Sixth Plan began on 1 April 1980.

s: The socialistic pattern of society was associated with which of the following sequence of developments?
o: Avadi Congress in 1955, followed by the Second Plan and IPR 1956
Second Plan in 1956, followed by Avadi Congress in 1958
Avadi Congress in 1961, followed by the Third Plan and IPR 1965
First Plan in 1951, followed by Avadi Congress in 1955 and IPR 1970
x: The socialistic pattern of society was adopted at the Avadi Congress in 1955 and was subsequently reflected in the Second Plan and the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.

s: Which of the following is regarded as the principal objective of planning in India?
x: Economic growth is the principal objective of planning, while modernisation, self-reliance and social justice are subsidiary or complementary objectives.

s: Which of the following is one of the four long-term objectives of Indian planning?
x: The four long-term objectives are growth, modernisation, self-reliance and social justice.

s: At which Congress session was the socialistic pattern of society adopted?
x: The Avadi Congress (1955) adopted it; it shaped the Second Plan and IPR 1956.

s: What was the declared aim of planning in India?
o: A rapid rise in the standard of living with employment for all
Complete state ownership of all industries
x: Planning aimed at a rapid rise in the standard of living through efficient use of resources, more production and employment for all.

s: Which of the following is NOT a chief objective of planning in India?
x: Growth, removal of poverty and self-reliance are listed objectives; 'to achieve social equality' is not a chief objective.

s: A long-term perspective plan covering 1985–2000 accompanied which Five-Year Plan?
x: A long-term perspective plan for 1985–2000 accompanied the Seventh Plan.

s: What does perspective planning refer to?
o: A plan revised every year and extended by one year
Long-term planning over 15–20 years or more
Planning by binding orders of a central authority
Planning limited to the current financial year
x: Perspective planning covers 15–20 years or more; five-year and annual plans are carved out of it.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's GSDP target for 2047-48 under Swarna Andhra Vision 2047?
x: AP's perspective target is a GSDP of Rs 308.11 lakh crore by 2047-48; Rs 31 lakh crore is the 2030 target.

s: How many 'Padi Sutralu' (guiding principles) does Andhra Pradesh's Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 have?
x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 is built on ten 'Padi Sutralu'.

s: What annual growth rate did Andhra Pradesh set in February 2026 to reach a GSDP of Rs 31 lakh crore by 2030?
x: On 10 February 2026 AP set targets of 15% annual growth, GSDP of Rs 31 lakh crore and per capita income of Rs 5.15 lakh by 2030.

s: Who conceived PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas)?
x: PURA (2003) was the idea of A.P.J. Abdul Kalam; it was announced by PM Vajpayee.

s: To which sector did the First Five Year Plan (from 1 April 1951) give the highest priority?
x: Facing foodgrain imports and inflation, the First Plan gave top priority to agriculture.

s: What actual growth rate did the First Five-Year Plan achieve?
x: The First Plan achieved 3.6 per cent growth against its target of 2.1 per cent.

s: With which Plan did the target-group approach in Indian planning begin?
x: It began with the Fourth Plan (1969), with programmes like SFDA, MFAL and DPAP; IRDP came in the Sixth Plan.

s: Besides self-reliance, what did the Fifth Five Year Plan aim at?
o: Raising the consumption of the poor
x: The Fifth Plan aimed at self-reliance and higher consumption of the poor; the Fourth emphasised weaker sections.

s: Which of the following pairs of Plan and main thrust is correctly matched?
o: First Plan – Removal of poverty and self-reliance
Third Plan – Agriculture, irrigation and power
Second Plan – Rapid industrialisation and socialistic pattern
x: The Second Plan stressed rapid industrialisation; the First focused on agriculture, irrigation and power, the Third on self-reliance and food self-sufficiency, and the Fifth on poverty removal.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ninth Plan — Rapid industrialisation under the Mahalanobis model
Sixth Plan — Poverty alleviation and Minimum Needs Programme
Twelfth Plan — Seven Basic Minimum Services
Seventh Plan — Agriculture, irrigation and power as its main thrust
x: The Sixth Plan emphasised poverty alleviation and the Minimum Needs Programme. Seven Basic Minimum Services were associated with the Ninth Plan, while the Twelfth Plan stressed faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth.

s: The approach during the First, Second and Third Plans was based on the belief that economic growth would eventually reach the poor. What was this approach known as?
x: The First to Third Plans followed the trickle-down approach, assuming that the benefits of growth would reach poorer sections.

s: The SFDA, MFAL and DPAP programmes belonged to which approach?
x: SFDA, MFAL and DPAP came under the target-group approach of the Fourth Plan.

s: The 'Seven Basic Minimum Services' were the thrust of which Plan?
x: The Ninth Plan (1997-2002) stressed the Seven Basic Minimum Services.

s: What was the main thrust of the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66)?
x: The Third Plan aimed at self-reliance, food self-sufficiency and import substitution.

s: Which programme of 1952 belonged to the trickle-down phase of Indian planning?
x: The First to Third Plans followed the trickle-down approach; the Community Development Programme (1952) belongs to this phase.

s: According to the Harrod-Domar logic applied to the First Plan, on what does growth depend primarily?
o: The savings rate and the capital-output ratio
The foreign exchange rate and population density
The tax rate and import quota
The wage rate and literacy rate
x: The Harrod-Domar framework links growth to the savings rate and the capital-output ratio.

s: The Second Five Year Plan was based on which growth model?
x: The Second Plan used the Feldman-Mahalanobis model; Harrod-Domar was the First Plan's.

s: Who put forward the wage goods model as an alternative to the Mahalanobis strategy?
x: C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda proposed expanding wage goods first.

s: Which of the following was NOT given priority under the Mahalanobis strategy?
x: Mahalanobis stressed heavy industry, the public sector and import substitution; export promotion was not a priority.

s: In which year did a foreign-exchange crisis force cuts in the Mahalanobis-based Second Plan?
x: The foreign-exchange crisis forced cuts in 1958; the model was replaced by the Third Plan (1961).

s: In the financing of India's Five Year Plans, what did 'deficit financing' mean?
o: Borrowing from the RBI, that is, money creation
x: Deficit financing was borrowing from the RBI; foreign aid and domestic savings (including market borrowing and PSU surpluses) were the other sources.

s: Which Plan aimed to reduce India's dependence on foreign aid?
x: The Fourth Plan aimed to reduce dependence on foreign aid.

s: What was the largest source of public sector outlay in the Eighth Five Year Plan?
x: In the Eighth Plan, government (market) borrowings were the largest source of public sector outlay (Rs 2,02,255 crore, 46.6%); deficit financing was only Rs 20,000 crore.

s: What is planning that works through binding quotas and allocation called?
x: Imperative planning uses binding quotas; indicative planning only guides the private sector.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the type of planning?
o: Imperative planning — mixed ownership and non-binding signals
Indicative planning — state or collective ownership only
Imperative planning — USSR under Stalin and China
x: The USSR under Stalin, beginning with the 1928 planning experience, and China are examples associated with imperative planning. Indicative planning is generally associated with mixed economies and market guidance.

s: From which Plan did India shift from imperative features towards indicative planning?
o: First Plan after the adoption of the Harrod-Domar model
Fourth Plan after the Green Revolution
Twelfth Plan after the abolition of the Planning Commission
x: India shifted to indicative planning from the Eighth Plan, covering 1992–97, following the economic reforms of 1991.

s: What happens to the market mechanism in imperative planning?
x: Imperative planning replaces the market by command; indicative planning improves it.

s: Which country first adopted imperative planning in 1928?
x: The USSR under Stalin began imperative planning in 1928.

s: What is the allocation of resources in real terms (materials, manpower and output targets) called?
x: Physical planning allocates in real terms; allocation in money terms is financial planning.

s: What does decentralised planning mean?
o: All decisions are taken by one central authority
Decisions are distributed to lower governments or private units within a broad policy
The plan is revised every year and extended by one year
The plan covers a period of 15–20 years
x: Decentralised planning distributes decision-making to lower governments or private units within a broad policy framework; centralised planning concentrates it in one authority.

s: Planning in which incentives guide private units, instead of command, is called planning by:
x: Planning by inducement uses incentives (indicative); planning by direction uses command (imperative).

s: What is the allocation of resources in money terms called?
x: Financial planning allocates in money terms; physical planning in real terms.

s: What type of planning is it when plans are made through elected bodies and with the consent of the people, as in India?
x: India follows democratic planning, where plans pass through elected bodies and consent, unlike totalitarian state command.

s: Which model prioritised agriculture and wage goods?
x: The wage-goods model favoured agriculture and wage goods; Mahalanobis prioritised heavy industry and capital goods.

s: By what other name is the Second Five Year Plan model, which saw scarcity of capital goods as the main bottleneck, known?
x: It is the Feldman-Mahalanobis model; the Harrod-Domar model saw limited savings as the bottleneck.

s: Which of the following pairs of plan model and its main bottleneck is correctly matched?
x: Harrod-Domar saw limited savings as the bottleneck; Mahalanobis saw capital goods and the wage-goods model saw food.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Solow-Swan model is correct?
o: It is a neoclassical model based on a Cobb-Douglas production function.
It is another name for the wage-goods model.
It was the model underlying the Second Five Year Plan.
It was the model underlying the First Five Year Plan.
x: The Solow-Swan model is a neoclassical growth model built on a Cobb-Douglas production function. No Indian Five Year Plan in the given list was based on it.

s: Which of the following pairs of Five-Year Plan and model is correctly matched?
x: The Fourth Plan used the Allen Manne–Ashok Rudra model; the First was Harrod-Domar, the Third Sandy-Chakravarty and the Fifth the Dhar model.

s: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) was based on which model?
x: The Third Plan followed the Sandy-Chakravarty model with import substitution.

s: On which model was the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79) based?
x: The Fifth Plan was based on the Dhar model.

s: Which of the following models was NOT the basis of any Indian Five Year Plan?
x: The neoclassical Solow-Swan model was never used by an Indian plan; the others underlay the First, Fourth and Third Plans.

s: On whose model was the Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74) based?
x: The Fourth Plan used the Allen Manne – Ashok Rudra model along with the Gadgil strategy.

s: Which Five Year Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model?
x: The First Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model, with modifications.

s: Which Five Year Plan was also called the 'Gadgil Yojana'?
x: The Third Plan (1961-66), based on the Sandy-Chakravarty model, is called the Gadgil Yojana.

s: Which Five Year Plan followed the Gadgil strategy of growth with stability?
x: The Fourth Plan (1969-74) was based on the Manne-Rudra model and the Gadgil strategy of growth with stability.

s: What did the Visvesvaraya Plan (1934) aim at?
o: Doubling per capita income in 15 years
Doubling national income within a decade
Trebling national income within a decade
x: Visvesvaraya's plan aimed to double national income in a decade through industrialisation; trebling in 15 years was the Bombay Plan.

s: Which of the following did the Bombay Plan (1944) favour?
o: A significant role for the State
x: The Bombay Plan wanted a significant State role, public sector development and protection of infant industries.

s: What did the People's Plan advocate?
o: Marxist socialism with equal weight to agriculture and industry
State-led industrialisation with protection of infant industries
Priority to heavy industry under the public sector
x: The People's Plan advocated Marxist socialism, stressed basic necessities and gave agriculture and industry equal weight.

s: Who prepared the People's Plan (1945)?
x: M.N. Roy prepared the People's Plan in 1945; the Bombay Plan, Gandhian Plan and Dalal's Planning and Development Department belong to 1944.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gandhian Plan — agriculture, cottage and village industries
People’s Plan — self-contained villages and Trusteeship
Bombay Plan — Marxist socialism and basic necessities
Sarvodaya Plan — licensing to protect infant industries
x: The Gandhian Plan emphasised agriculture, cottage and village industries, decentralisation, Swadeshi, Sarvodaya and Trusteeship.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's planning milestones:
1. The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938.
2. The Bombay and Gandhian Plans came in 1944.
3. The People's Plan came before the Bombay Plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The NPC dates to 1938 and the Bombay and Gandhian Plans to 1944; the People's Plan came later, in 1945.

s: Who headed the Advisory Planning Board of 1946?
x: K.C. Neogi headed the 1946 board; Mahalanobis was architect of the Second Plan and founded the ISI in 1931.

s: Under which title was the Bombay Plan published?
o: An Economic Programme for Self-contained Villages
A Plan of Economic Development for India
x: The Bombay Plan was titled “A Plan of Economic Development for India.”

s: The Bombay Plan (1944) aimed to raise national income how many times in 15 years?
x: The Bombay Plan aimed to treble national income in 15 years; the Visvesvaraya Plan aimed to double it in a decade.

s: How many Bombay industrialists signed the Bombay Plan?
x: The Bombay Plan was drawn up by 8 Bombay industrialists, including J.R.D. Tata and G.D. Birla.

s: Who chaired the National Planning Committee (1938), set up under Subhas Chandra Bose?
x: The NPC was set up under Bose and chaired by Nehru.

s: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Planning'?
x: M. Visvesvaraya, whose 'Planned Economy for India' (1934) was the first planning blueprint, is called the Father of Indian Planning.

s: In which year did Shriman Narayan Agarwal put forward the Gandhian Plan?
x: The Gandhian Plan came in 1944, the same year as the Bombay Plan.

s: Which slogan of the 1990s is said to echo M.N. Roy's People's Plan?
x: The People's Plan's stress on basic needs was echoed in the 1990s slogan 'reforms with a human face'.

s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Mahalanobis strategy?
x: The strategy emphasised import substitution, self-reliance and a dominant public sector. Exports and export promotion were neglected rather than depended upon.

s: The Mahalanobis strategy is often described as a strategy of:
o: Balanced growth based equally on all sectors
Unbalanced growth centred on heavy industry
x: The strategy is described as unbalanced growth because it gave priority to basic and heavy industries while neglecting agriculture, exports and consumer goods.

s: From what level to what level did the Mahalanobis strategy seek to raise the investment rate?
x: The strategy aimed to raise investment from 7 per cent to 11 per cent of national income.

s: What did the Mahalanobis model assume?
o: Foreign trade as the central source of growth
x: The model assumed a closed economy and neglected agriculture; foreign trade was not central to it.

s: What growth did the Second Five Year Plan achieve against its target?
o: 5.27 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent
4.5 per cent against a target of 4.27 per cent
3.27 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent
4.27 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent
x: The Second Five Year Plan achieved 4.27 per cent growth against its target of 4.5 per cent.

s: Under the Second Five Year Plan, with the manufacture of what was Chittaranjan associated?
x: Chittaranjan made locomotives; Perambur made coaches and Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela were steel plants.

s: How many sectors did the Mahalanobis model have?
x: Its four sectors were capital goods, factory consumer goods, household/small-scale consumer goods and services.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mahalanobis model:
1. Feldman (1928) and Mahalanobis (1953) developed it independently.
2. It left consumer goods to the small and cottage sector.
3. It gave top priority to agriculture.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the model gave priority to the capital goods sector and neglected agriculture.

s: Which of the following was NOT neglected by the Mahalanobis model?
x: Heavy industry was its priority; agriculture, consumer goods and exports were neglected.

s: Which of the following steel plants was set up under the Second Five Year Plan?
x: Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela steel plants came up under the Mahalanobis-based Second Plan.

s: What did the Perambur unit, set up under the Second Five Year Plan, manufacture?
x: Under the Second Plan, Perambur made railway coaches and Chittaranjan made locomotives.

s: In which year did Stalin's USSR, whose system is described as imperative planning, begin five-year plans?
x: The USSR began five-year plans in 1928; India follows indicative planning.

s:
Consider the following statements about types of planning:
1. India follows indicative planning.
2. Stalin's USSR followed indicative planning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India follows indicative planning; Stalin's USSR, which began plans in 1928, followed imperative planning.

s: In the Harrod-Domar model, other factors remaining constant, when does growth rise?
x: Growth depends positively on the savings rate and negatively on the capital-output ratio.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Capital Output Ratio is incorrect?
o: A high COR means that investment produces relatively less output.
A high COR indicates lower capital productivity.
A low COR indicates higher productivity of capital.
A low COR means that more capital is needed for each unit of output.
x: Option D is incorrect: a low COR means less capital is needed per unit of output, so capital is more productive. Needing more capital per unit means a high COR.

s: What does a decrease in the Capital-Output Ratio mean per unit of output?
x: A lower COR means less capital is needed per unit of output, which raises growth potential.

s: In the Harrod-Domar equation g = s / k, what does 'k' stand for?
x: In g = s / k, g is the growth rate, s the savings rate and k the capital-output ratio.

s: What was the main reason for the success of the First Five Year Plan?
o: Good harvests in its last two years
x: Despite refugees, food shortage and inflation, the First Plan succeeded mainly due to good harvests in its last two years.

s: What does a high Capital Output Ratio mean for the output produced by investment?
o: faster growth from the same savings
x: With a high COR each unit of investment yields relatively little output, so even high savings may give slow growth.

s: By which Act was the Indian Statistical Institute made an Institution of National Importance?
x: The Indian Statistical Institute was made an Institution of National Importance through the ISI Act of 1959.

s: When was the first round of the National Sample Survey, recommended by the National Income Committee, held?
x: The first NSS round was in 1950–51; Mahalanobis chaired the National Income Committee (1949).

s: Whose birth anniversary is observed as National Statistics Day on 29 June?
x: National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June, the birth anniversary of P.C. Mahalanobis, since 2007.

s: In which year was the Indian Statistical Institute founded in Kolkata?
x: P.C. Mahalanobis founded the ISI on 17 December 1931; the ISI Act came in 1959.

s: Since which year has National Statistics Day been observed in India?
x: National Statistics Day, 29 June, has been observed since 2007.

s: P.C. Mahalanobis is known as the architect of which Five Year Plan?
x: Mahalanobis was the architect of the Second Plan (1956-61).

s: Who chaired the National Income Committee of 1949, which recommended the National Sample Survey?
x: P.C. Mahalanobis chaired the National Income Committee (1949); it recommended the NSS, whose first round was held in 1950-51.

s: What was the theme of National Statistics Day 2026?
o: Unlocking the Potential of Administrative Data
x: National Statistics Day (29 June) 2026 had the theme 'Unlocking the Potential of Administrative Data'.

s: In which year was P.C. Mahalanobis awarded the Padma Vibhushan?
x: Mahalanobis received the Padma Vibhushan in 1968; he became FRS in 1945.

s: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2026, seeks to replace which Act?
o: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
x: The ISI Bill, 2026 was introduced on 2 August 2026 to replace the ISI Act, 1959.

s: To which parliamentary committee was the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 referred?
o: Select Committee of the Rajya Sabha
x: On 1 September 2026 the ISI Bill, 2026 was referred to the Standing Committee on Finance.

s: In Gandhian thought, what does 'Ram Rajya' primarily denote?
o: A state controlled by religious institutions
A monarchy headed by a hereditary ruler
Rule based on pure moral authority and justice for the poorest
x: Ram Rajya refers to rule founded on moral authority and justice for the poorest; it does not mean the establishment of a Hindu state.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gandhian Constitution for Free India — M.N. Roy
x: The *Gandhian Constitution for Free India* was authored by Shriman Narayan Agarwal. M.N. Roy authored the People's Plan.

s: Who wrote 'Gandhian Constitution for Free India'?
x: Shriman Narayan Agarwal wrote it, not M.N. Roy; Charan Singh wrote 'The Gandhian Blue Print'.

s: Which of the following was emphasised in the Janata Government's alternative strategy?
x: The Janata strategy stressed agriculture, rural development, employment, small and cottage industries and minimum needs rather than heavy industry.

s: For which period did the Janata Government, after ending the Fifth Plan a year early, adopt a Rolling Plan?
x: The Rolling Plan covered 1978–80, following a concept advocated by Gunnar Myrdal.

s: Whose concept was the Rolling Plan adopted by the Janata Government (1978-80)?
x: The Rolling Plan, adopted after the Fifth Plan was ended a year early, was Gunnar Myrdal's concept.

s: Who put forward the wage-goods model?
x: The wage-goods model was put forward by C.N. Vakil and P.R. Brahmananda in 1956.

s: According to the wage-goods model, what is the main constraint on economic expansion?
o: Wage goods such as food and essential consumer goods
x: The wage-goods model treats the supply of food and essential consumer goods, not capital goods, as the real constraint on expansion.

s: Which book is associated with the wage-goods model?
o: A Plan of Economic Development for India
x: Vakil and Brahmananda put forward the wage-goods model in their 1956 work, Planning for an Expanding Economy.

s: In the wage-goods model, more wage goods would allow which group to be put to productive work?
x: Vakil and Brahmananda argued that more wage goods would let the disguised unemployed be put to productive work.

s: In contrast to Mahalanobis, the wage-goods model held that the real constraint was NOT the supply of:
x: The wage-goods model saw food and essential consumer goods as the constraint, not capital goods.

s: Which of the following pairs of Five Year Plan and objective is correctly matched?
o: Second Plan – Growth with stability and progressive self-reliance
Fifth Plan – Self-reliant and self-generating economy
Third Plan – Self-reliant and self-generating economy
Fourth Plan – Removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao)
x: The Third Plan aimed at a self-reliant, self-generating economy; growth with stability was the Fourth Plan's aim.

s: Which of the following statements about the First Five Year Plan is incorrect?
o: Its primary priority was heavy industry.
Its major focus included food production, rehabilitation and price stability.
x: Option B is incorrect: the First Plan put agriculture first, along with food, rehabilitation after Partition, and price stability. Heavy industry was the Second Plan's priority.

s:
Assertion (A): The Fifth Five Year Plan focused on Garibi Hatao, employment, justice and self-reliance.
Reason (R): The Fifth Five Year Plan covered the period 1974–79.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: the Fifth Plan (1974–79) focused on Garibi Hatao, jobs, justice and self-reliance. Its dates do not explain its aims, so R does not explain A.

s: In which year did the Green Revolution begin during the Plan Holiday?
x: The Green Revolution began in 1966–67, when only Annual Plans were implemented.

s: From which Five Year Plan were anti-poverty programmes first started in India?
x: Serious concern for unemployment began and anti-poverty programmes were first started in the Fifth Plan (1974-79).

s: Which Five Year Plan is known as the 'Mahalanobis Plan'?
x: The Second Plan is called the Mahalanobis Plan; real planning and rapid industrialisation began with it.

s: Which Five Year Plan aimed at 'zero net foreign aid' along with self-reliance and control of inflation?
x: The Fifth Plan (1974-79) aimed at removal of poverty, self-reliance, control of inflation and zero net foreign aid.

s: In which year was the Fourth Five Year Plan finally launched after the Plan Holiday?
x: After three Annual Plans (1966-69), the Fourth Plan was finally launched in 1969.

s: 'Garibi Hatao', which became the basic objective of the Fifth Plan, was Indira Gandhi's slogan in which elections?
x: Garibi Hatao was Indira Gandhi's slogan in the 1971 elections and became the Fifth Plan's basic objective.

s: How many Annual Plans made up the Plan Holiday of 1966-69?
x: The Plan Holiday (1 April 1966 to 31 March 1969) had three Annual Plans.

s: With which Five Year Plan are the Bhakra Nangal and Hirakud projects associated?
x: The First Plan focused on agriculture, irrigation and power, with projects like Bhakra Nangal and Hirakud.

s: Which Five Year Plan had the objective of 'growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance'?
x: The Fourth Plan (1969-74) aimed at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.

s: Who prepared the final draft of the Fifth Five Year Plan?
x: The Fifth Plan (1974-79) was based on the Dhar model; its final draft was prepared by D.P. Dhar.

s: What was the focus sector of the Second Five Year Plan (1956-61)?
x: The Second Plan gave maximum emphasis to heavy and basic industries under the Nehru-Mahalanobis model.

s: The Eighth Five Year Plan was based on which of the following models?
x: The Eighth Five Year Plan, covering 1992–97, was associated with the John W. Miller model.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ninth Plan — Growth with social justice and equity
Seventh Plan — Food, work and productivity
Fifth Plan — Removal of poverty and self-reliance
x: Human resource development was the principal objective of the Eighth Plan, whereas the Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and doubling of per capita income in ten years.

s: Doubling of per capita income in ten years was an aim of which Five Year Plan?
x: The Tenth Plan targeted 8 per cent GDP growth and sought to double per capita income within ten years.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Eighth Five Year Plan covered 1992–97 and focused on growth with human development.
The Eleventh Five Year Plan covered 2007–12 and focused on growth with social justice.
The Twelfth Five Year Plan covered 2012–17 and focused on faster, sustainable and inclusive growth.
The Tenth Five Year Plan covered 2002–07 and focused on faster growth and development.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Eleventh Plan (2007–12) aimed at faster and more inclusive growth. 'Growth with social justice' was the Ninth Plan's aim.

s: Which Five Year Plan had 'poverty eradication and technological self-reliance' as its main objective?
x: The Sixth Plan (1980-85) aimed at poverty eradication and technological self-reliance.

s: Under which government was the Ninth Five Year Plan, 'Growth with Social Justice and Equity', formulated?
x: The Ninth Plan (1997-2002) was formulated under the United Front Government; the NDC gave final approval on 19 February 1999.

s: Employment was the main thrust of which Five Year Plan?
x: The Seventh Plan's thrust was employment; the First stressed agriculture and irrigation, the Second heavy industry and the Sixth power.

s: Which Five Year Plan was the first to focus on gender issues and inter-State as well as intra-State inequalities?
x: The Sixth Plan was the first plan to focus on gender issues and inter-State and intra-State inequalities.

s: Which sector was placed first in the Eleventh Plan, with education receiving the highest emphasis?
x: The Eleventh Plan placed the social sector first, with education at the top of its priorities.

s: Which of the following pairs (Plan – actual growth rate) is correctly matched?
x: The First Plan achieved 3.6% growth. The Second Plan achieved 4.27%, the Third Plan 2.2% and the Plan Holiday 3.69%.

s: What was the approximate GDP growth rate of India in 1950-51?
x: GDP grew about 3.6% in 1950-51. 1.1% was the growth of 1990-91, 2.1% was the First Plan's target, and -5.2% (not +5.2%) was the contraction of 1979.

s: What was the average growth over the First to Eleventh Plans, against roughly 1 per cent before Independence?
x: Plan-period growth averaged about 4.5%; agriculture grew 2-3% and industry about 6-8%.

s: Which group contains only those Five Year Plans that exceeded their GDP growth targets?
o: First, Second, Fifth, Seventh and Eighth
Second, Fifth, Sixth, Eighth and Ninth
First, Third, Sixth, Seventh and Tenth
First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth
x: The First, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth Plans achieved growth above their respective targets.

s: Which of the following plans recorded the lowest actual GDP growth?
x: The Third Plan recorded actual growth of about 2.2 per cent, the lowest among the listed plans.

s: Leaving aside the Covid-19 contraction of 2020-21, in which year did India record its lowest GDP growth since 1961?
x: 1979 recorded the lowest growth since 1961, about -5.2%, owing to drought and the second oil shock. 1965-66 and 1972-73 were other negative years but less severe, and 1991-92 grew below 1% but did not contract as sharply. Only the pandemic year 2020-21 (-5.8%) was worse.

s: What was the actual average annual growth rate achieved during the Eighth Five Year Plan?
x: The Eighth Plan (1992-97) achieved 6.8% growth against a target of 5.6%.

s: In which year did India record GDP growth of 8.2 per cent, after a poor-monsoon year of about 4 per cent?
x: GDP grew about 4% in 2002-03 (poor monsoon) and 8.2% in 2003-04.

s: What was the average annual GDP growth recorded during the Twelfth Five Year Plan?
x: The Twelfth Plan recorded GDP growth of about 6.7% a year; per capita NNI grew about 5.3%.

s: What was the actual growth rate achieved in the Eleventh Five Year Plan, the highest among all the plans?
x: The Eleventh Plan achieved 8.0% growth against a 9% target, the highest of all plans.

s: Which period recorded the highest average GDP growth in India?
x: The highest average growth came in 2004-05 to 2012-13, with a boom peak of about 8.5% in 2003-08.

s: What GDP growth target for the Twelfth Five Year Plan was finally approved by the National Development Council in December 2012?
x: The Approach Paper proposed 9%, but the NDC in December 2012 approved a target of 8%.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Twelfth Five Year Plan:
1. Its Approach Paper proposed a GDP growth target of 9 per cent.
2. The National Development Council approved a lower target of 8 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Twelfth Plan target was 9% in the Approach Paper and was cut to 8% by the NDC in December 2012.

s: What average annual growth did the Tenth Five Year Plan achieve against its target of 8 per cent?
x: The Tenth Plan (2002-07) achieved 7.6% against a target of 8% (cut to 7% at mid-term).

s: What growth rate did the Ninth Five Year Plan achieve against its target of 6.5 per cent?
x: The Ninth Plan (1997-2002) grew 5.4% against its 6.5% target.

s: During which Five Year Plan was the Twenty-Point Programme introduced?
x: The Twenty-Point Programme and the Minimum Needs Programme came in the Fifth Plan; DPAP in the Fourth.

s: Which was the first Five Year Plan to set monitorable targets?
x: The Tenth Plan (2002-07) first set monitorable targets; the Eleventh extended them.

s: The Community Development Programme was introduced during which Five Year Plan?
x: The Community Development Programme was introduced in 1952 during the First Five Year Plan.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Command Area Development was introduced in 1974–75 during the Fifth Plan. IRDP and NABARD belong to the Sixth Plan, while the Women's Component Plan belongs to the Ninth Plan.

s: The Drought Prone Area Programme was introduced in which Five Year Plan?
x: The DPAP and other target-group programmes began in the Fourth Plan.

s: In the first year of which Plan was the Minimum Needs Programme launched?
x: The Minimum Needs Programme began in the first year of the Fifth Plan.

s: Which of the following pairs of programme and Five Year Plan is correctly matched?
x: IRDP came in the Sixth Plan; CADA was a Fifth Plan programme and Jawahar Rozgar Yojana came in the Seventh.

s: The Command Area Development Programme (1974-75) belongs to which Five Year Plan?
x: CADA was started in 1974-75, in the Fifth Plan.

s: In which Five Year Plan was the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana launched by merging NREP and RLEGP?
x: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana was launched on 1 April 1989, in the Seventh Plan.

s: During which Five Year Plan was NABARD set up in 1982?
x: IRDP, NREP and NABARD (1982) belong to the Sixth Plan (1980-85).

s: In which Five Year Plan was the National Horticulture Mission launched in May 2005?
x: The National Horticulture Mission (May 2005) and NRHM (2005) came in the Tenth Plan, not the Eleventh.

s: In which year was the Second Five Year Plan introduced?
x: The Second Plan began in 1956, the same year as the Industrial Policy Resolution.

s: Which sector received the largest allocation in the Twelfth Five Year Plan?
x: The Twelfth Plan gave its largest allocation, about 34.7%, to social services.

s: Which of the following was NOT a reason for pruning the Second Plan’s outlay?
o: A sustained fall in inflation caused by excess food production
x: The outlay was pruned because of food and capital shortages, inflation, unrealistic closed-economy assumptions and the 1957–58 foreign-exchange crisis. A sustained fall in inflation was not a reason.

s: Which of the following was a major criticism of the Nehru–Mahalanobis strategy?
o: It neglected agriculture and contributed to food shortages and inflation.
It relied excessively on labour-intensive small industries and created too many jobs.
It gave no importance to heavy industry.
x: The strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture, generating food shortages and inflation, and relying on capital-intensive heavy industry that created few jobs.

s: What was the planned public sector outlay of the Second Five Year Plan?
x: The planned public outlay was Rs 4,800 crore; the actual outlay was pruned to Rs 4,600 crore.

s: The Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy created few jobs mainly because it relied on:
x: Its capital-intensive heavy industry generated few jobs, a key criticism of the strategy.

s: Against a planned public sector outlay of Rs 4,800 crore, what was the actual outlay of the Second Five Year Plan?
x: The Second Plan's actual public outlay was Rs 4,600 crore (Rs 3,650 crore investment and Rs 950 crore current spending).

s: Which committee reviewed the plan/non-plan distinction during the Twelfth Plan?
x: The Rangarajan Committee reviewed it; the Twelfth Plan also cut the number of CSS, gave a flexi-fund and promoted social-sector PPPs.

s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the Eleventh Plan’s inclusive-growth strategy?
o: Complete withdrawal of the private sector
Access to health, education and skills
x: The Eleventh Plan envisaged continued reform and a competitive private sector; it did not propose its complete withdrawal. The other three were components of inclusive growth.

s: The Eleventh Plan's 27 national monitorable targets included how many State-level targets?
x: The Eleventh Plan set 27 national monitorable targets, including 13 at the State level.

s: Which of the following correctly states the Eleventh Plan's monitorable targets?
o: GDP growth 9%, agricultural growth 4%, IMR 28 and TFR 2.1
GDP growth 9%, agricultural growth 6%, IMR 30 and TFR 2.1
GDP growth 10%, agricultural growth 4%, IMR 20 and TFR 1.9
GDP growth 8%, agricultural growth 5%, IMR 25 and TFR 2.5
x: The Eleventh Plan targeted 9 per cent GDP growth, 4 per cent agricultural growth, an IMR of 28 and a TFR of 2.1. Its MMR target was 1 per 1,000 live births.

s: How many monitorable targets did the Twelfth Five Year Plan set?
x: The Twelfth Plan had 25 monitorable targets, against 27 in the Eleventh.

s: Which of the following was an aim of the Twelfth Five Year Plan?
o: Fewer Centrally Sponsored Schemes with a flexi-fund
x: The Twelfth Plan sought fewer CSS with a flexi-fund, besides reducing poverty and regional inequality.

s: What was the size of the Twelfth Five Year Plan?
x: The Twelfth Plan outlay was Rs 76,69,807 crore, against Rs 36,44,718 crore for the Eleventh.

s: What Infant Mortality Rate target did the Twelfth Five Year Plan set?
x: The Twelfth Plan targeted an IMR of 25; the Eleventh had targeted 28.

s: How many new jobs did the Eleventh Five Year Plan aim to create?
x: The Eleventh Plan aimed at 7 crore new jobs and a 10-point cut in the poverty head-count ratio.

s: Which of the following correctly describes Jalayagnam in Andhra Pradesh?
o: An irrigation mission launched in 2004 to complete major and medium projects
A financial inclusion scheme launched in 2015
A rural employment programme launched in 1990
An industrial corridor launched in 2007 to promote exports
x: Jalayagnam was an irrigation mission launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2004 for completing major and medium irrigation projects.

s: During the Eleventh Plan, Andhra Pradesh targeted 9.5 percent GSDP growth. What did it achieve?
x: AP achieved 5.28 percent GSDP growth; its industrial growth was 7.26 percent against a 10 percent target.

s: During the Eleventh Five Year Plan period in Andhra Pradesh, which sector received the first priority?
x: The social sector received the first priority in Andhra Pradesh during the Eleventh Plan. Education received the highest priority within the social sector.

s: In which year was the Gadgil formula for allocation of Central assistance introduced?
x: The Gadgil formula was introduced in 1969. It was later modified into the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula in 1991.

s: Under the Gadgil–Mukherjee formula, what weight did population carry?
x: Population got 60 percent, per capita income 25 percent, and fiscal performance and special problems 7.5 percent each.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the pattern of assistance to States?
o: Special Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
General Category States — 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan
Special Category States — 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan
x: Special Category States received assistance in the ratio of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan. General Category States received 30 percent grant and 70 percent loan.

s: Swarna Andhra @2047 identified Visakhapatnam and Amaravati as two of Andhra Pradesh's three economic regions. Which is the third?
x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 names three economic regions: Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Kurnool is not one of them.

s: In which year did Jawaharlal Nehru lay the foundation stone of the Nagarjuna Sagar dam?
x: Nehru laid the foundation on 10 December 1955; the dam was built from 1955 to 1967.

s: In which year did construction of the Srisailam power project in Andhra Pradesh begin?
x: Srisailam construction began in 1960 and the project opened in 1981.

s: In which year did Krishna water under the Telugu Ganga project reach Poondi (Chennai)?
x: The Telugu Ganga project was taken up in the 1980s and its water reached Poondi in 2004.

s: During the Eleventh Plan, what was the share of agriculture and allied sectors in Andhra Pradesh's GSDP?
x: Agriculture and allied sectors made up 21.27% of AP's GSDP in the Eleventh Plan.

s: In what grant : loan ratio was central plan assistance given to General Category States such as Andhra Pradesh?
x: General Category States got 30% grant and 70% loan; Special Category States got 90 : 10.

s: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, what weight did per capita income carry?
x: Population had 60%, per capita income 25%, and fiscal performance and special problems 7.5% each.

s: In which year did the Five Year Plan system in India end?
x: Five Year Plans ended in 2017, though plan-style credit and regional planning continue.

s: During the Eleventh Plan, Andhra Pradesh's industry grew by 7.26 per cent. What was its target?
x: In the Eleventh Plan, AP's industry grew 7.26% against a 10% target; GSDP grew 5.28% against 9.5%.

s: When was Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 launched?
x: Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 was launched on 13 December 2024, aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047.

s: What credit plan for Andhra Pradesh did NABARD's State Focus Paper 2026-27 project?
x: NABARD's AP State Focus Paper 2026-27 put the credit plan at Rs 5.11 lakh crore, about 20% higher.

s: Construction of the Srisailam power project in Andhra Pradesh began in 1960. In which year was it opened?
x: Srisailam construction began in 1960 and the project was opened in 1981.

s: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, the population of which Census was used?
x: The Gadgil-Mukherjee formula (1991) gave 60% weight to population as per the 1971 Census.

s: Under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula, what weight was given to fiscal performance?
x: Weights: population 60%, per capita income 25%, fiscal performance 7.5%, special problems 7.5%.

s: After whom is the Prakasam Barrage on the Krishna river at Vijayawada named?
x: The barrage is named after Tanguturi Prakasam, the first Chief Minister of Andhra State.

s: During which period was the present Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna at Vijayawada built?
x: The present barrage was built in 1954-57, replacing the old anicut of 1852-55.

s: The Third Five Year Plan was adversely affected primarily by which combination of events?
o: The 1966 devaluation and the abolition of the Planning Commission
The 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis and political instability
The 1971 war and the oil shock of 1973
The 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965–66 drought
x: The Third Plan was derailed by the wars of 1962 and 1965 and the severe drought of 1965–66. This led to the Plan Holiday during 1966–69.

s: With what was the postponement of the Eighth Five Year Plan mainly associated?
o: political instability and the balance-of-payments crisis of 1990–91
the termination of the Fifth Plan by the Janata government
x: Political instability and the 1990–91 balance-of-payments crisis postponed the Eighth Plan. Annual Plans were implemented during 1990–92.

s: Which government's Sixth Plan of 1978 came to be called the Rolling Plan?
x: The Janata government ended the Fifth Plan a year early and started its own Sixth Plan in 1978 as a Rolling Plan.

s: In which year was the Food Corporation of India established?
x: FCI was set up in 1965 and, with the Green Revolution and National Seeds Corporation, aided food self-sufficiency.

s: The State Bank of India originated from which institution during the First Plan period?
x: The State Bank of India was created from the Imperial Bank during the First Plan period.

s: Which of the following groups contains only industrial and scientific institutions associated with the expansion of India’s industrial base during planning?
o: FCI, NABARD, SBI and the Green Revolution
Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela and the IITs
NITI Aayog, Gadgil formula, SBI and FCI
x: Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela steel plants, along with Chittaranjan, Perambur and the IITs, formed part of the industrial and scientific base created during planning.

s: Poverty in India fell from 48.3% in 1977-78 to what level in 1983-84?
x: Poverty fell from 48.3% (1977-78) to 37.4% (1983-84), an achievement of planning.

s: Among the failures of Indian planning, where did regional imbalance persist?
x: Regional imbalance existed both across and within States, along with poverty, inequality and lagging employment growth.

s: Which Five Year Plan is described with the remark 'the poor became poorer'?
x: The Eighth Plan's record on poverty is summed up as 'the poor became poorer'.

s: Which of the following is NOT a failure of Indian planning?
x: Food self-sufficiency, through the Green Revolution and FCI, was an achievement; the others were failures.

s: What was the approximate average economic growth over Plans I to XI?
x: Average growth over Plans I to XI was about 4.5 per cent, compared with roughly 1 per cent before Independence.

s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement associated with planning in India?
x: Regional disparities persisted and therefore were a failure rather than an achievement. Planning did contribute to savings, investment, food security and scientific manpower.

s: Which of the following pairs about the outcome of planning in India is correctly matched?
x: Land reforms were poorly implemented and unequal land ownership persisted; income inequality widened.

s: What has been the chief drawback of economic planning in India?
x: The chief drawback was implementation failure, even though planning produced several measurable achievements.

s: With whom did Padma Desai co-author 'India: Planning for Industrialization' (1970)?
x: Padma Desai, a critic of India's planned economy and the first Asian woman to earn a Harvard Economics PhD, co-authored the 1970 work with Jagdish Bhagwati.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Planning and the Poor — Padma Desai
India: Planning for Industrialization — B.S. Minhas alone
Planning and the Poor — B.S. Minhas
India: Planning for Industrialization — Gulzarilal Nanda
x: B.S. Minhas authored Planning and the Poor in 1974. India: Planning for Industrialization was co-authored by Padma Desai and Jagdish Bhagwati.

s: Which critic of Indian planning was the first Asian woman to earn a PhD in Economics from Harvard?
x: Padma Desai, co-author of 'India: Planning for Industrialization', earned her Harvard Economics PhD in 1960.

s: Which of the following statements describes planning after 1991?
o: It ended immediately after the Seventh Plan.
It shifted from directed planning to indicative planning, signalling priority sectors while leaving investment largely to the private sector.
It was made a constitutional requirement for all state governments.
It shifted from indicative planning to complete state direction of private investment.
x: After 1991, planning became indicative: it signalled priority sectors while private investment played a larger role. Planning was not a constitutional requirement.

s:
Consider the following statements about planning in India:
1. Planning is a constitutional requirement.
2. After 1991, planning became indicative, showing priority sectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Planning is not a constitutional requirement; after 1991 it moved from directed to indicative.

s: Why were Five Year Plans continued in India even after the move to a market economy in 1991?
o: The Finance Commission required a plan document
They gave a long-term perspective to the economy
The private sector had been abolished
x: Plans were kept after 1991 because they give a long-term perspective in a market economy; planning is not a constitutional requirement.

s: In which year was the National Development Council established?
x: The NDC was established in 1952, two years after the Planning Commission (1950).

s: Which institutional development ended the system of discretionary plan grants in India?
o: Establishment of the National Development Council
Introduction of the Goods and Services Tax
x: The abolition of the Planning Commission ended the system of discretionary plan grants. NITI Aayog was not created as a body with comparable financial powers.

s: Which statement regarding the National Development Council is correct?
o: It was established in 1952 and its functions have passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council, although a formal abolition resolution remains pending.
It was a constitutional body established under the Constitution.
It was formally abolished before the establishment of NITI Aayog.
It replaced NITI Aayog as the principal fund allocator in 2015.
x: The National Development Council was established in 1952 and is now inactive. Its functions have passed to NITI Aayog’s Governing Council, but formal abolition is still pending.

s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog primarily performs which function?
o: Approving the annual plan outlays of States
Allocating plan funds to Union Ministries
Coordinating policy among the Centre and the States
x: The Governing Council coordinates policy between the Centre and the States; NITI Aayog has no financial powers to redistribute plan grants.

s: On which date did NITI Aayog replace the Planning Commission?
x: NITI Aayog was set up by a government resolution on 1 January 2015.

s: Who was the last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
x: M.S. Ahluwalia was the last Deputy Chairman before the Commission was dissolved in 2014.

s: On which date did the last Five Year Plan of India end?
x: The Twelfth Plan (2012-17), the last, ended on 31 March 2017.

s: At the 11th NITI Aayog Governing Council meeting in June 2026, what did the Prime Minister urge States to estimate?
x: At the 11th Governing Council (June 2026), the PM urged States to estimate district-level GDP.

s: In which year was the Planning Commission dissolved?
x: The Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014 and NITI Aayog replaced it on 1 January 2015.

s: Up to which year does NITI Aayog's 15-year vision document run?
x: The 15-year vision runs up to 2030, with a 7-year strategy and 3-year action agenda.

s: What was the period of NITI Aayog's 3-year action agenda?
x: The 3-year action agenda (released 1 August 2017) covered 2017-18 to 2019-20.

s: Which period did the 7-year strategy that replaced the Five Year Plans cover?
x: The 7-year strategy ran from 2017-18 to 2023-24.

s: What was the focus sector of India's First Five Year Plan?
x: The First Plan gave priority to agriculture and irrigation.

s: What growth rate (per cent) did the Third Five Year Plan achieve against a target of 5.6 per cent?
x: The Third Plan grew only 2.2% against its 5.6% target, hit by the 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965-66 droughts.

s: The Plan Holiday of 1966-69 followed the failure of which Five Year Plan?
x: The Third Plan's failure (2.2% vs 5.6%) led to the Plan Holiday of 1966-69.

s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the Third Plan's failure?
x: The Third Plan was hit by the 1962 and 1965 wars and the 1965-66 droughts; the 1971 war affected the Fourth Plan.

s: Which strategy did the Fourth Five Year Plan, aiming at growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance, follow?
x: The Fourth Plan followed the Gadgil strategy, which emphasised growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.

s: How many banks were nationalised in 1969, during the Fourth Plan period?
x: Fourteen banks were nationalised in 1969, during the Fourth Plan.

s: What annual export growth did the Fourth Five Year Plan target?
x: The Fourth Plan's Gadgil strategy targeted exports growing about 7% a year.

s: Against a target of 5.7%, what growth did the Fourth Five Year Plan achieve?
x: The Fourth Plan achieved 3.3% against 5.7% because of droughts and the 1971 war.

s: Under central plan assistance, in what ratio did Special Category States receive grant and loan?
x: Special Category States got 90% grant and 10% loan; General Category got 30 : 70.

s: In which year was the Gadgil formula for allocating central assistance to State plans replaced by the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula?
x: The Gadgil formula (1969) gave way to the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula in 1991.

s: Which Five Year Plan was finally launched in 1969, after the Plan Holiday?
x: After the Plan Holiday of 1966-69, the Fourth Plan was launched in 1969 with the Gadgil strategy.

s: The Fourth Five Year Plan grew only 3.3 per cent against a target of 5.7 per cent. What was the main reason?
x: The Fourth Plan fell short because of droughts and the 1971 war.

s: What annual agricultural growth did the Fourth Five Year Plan target?
x: The Fourth Plan targeted 5% annual agricultural growth; about 7% a year was its export growth target.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NITI – National Institution for Transforming India
Arvind Panagariya – first CEO of NITI Aayog
x: NITI stands for National Institution for Transforming India. NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 and DMEO on 18 September 2015; Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairman, while Sindhushree Khullar was the first CEO.

s: How was NITI Aayog created?
x: NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional advisory body created by an executive Cabinet resolution.

s: Who chairs the Zonal Councils, the statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
x: Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister; a NITI Aayog representative attends as an adviser.

s: Which of the following is a statutory body?
x: Zonal Councils are statutory, set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. NITI Aayog and the Planning Commission are non-statutory; the Finance Commission is constitutional.

s: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
x: The Finance Commission (Article 280) is constitutional; NITI Aayog and the Planning Commission are non-statutory and Zonal Councils are statutory.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NITI Aayog's office-holders?
o: The Vice-Chairperson and the CEO are separate posts
The Vice-Chairperson also serves as the CEO
The CEO holds the rank of Secretary to the Government of India
The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister
x: The VC and CEO are separate posts; there is no Vice-Chairman-cum-CEO.

s: Who was the first Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog?
x: Sindhushree Khullar was the first CEO of NITI Aayog. Amitabh Kant and B.V.R. Subrahmanyam served later as CEOs.

s: Who succeeded Arvind Panagariya as Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in 2017?
x: Rajiv Kumar (2017) followed Arvind Panagariya (2015); Suman K. Bery came in May 2022 and Ashok Kumar Lahiri in April 2026.

s: Who became Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog on 25 April 2026?
x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri, a former Chief Economic Adviser, took over from Suman K. Bery on 25 April 2026.

s: Who was appointed CEO of NITI Aayog in July 2026 for two years?
