x: Anurag Jain, a 1989-batch IAS officer and former Madhya Pradesh Chief Secretary, became CEO in July 2026.

s: Who, the first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog, later chaired the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Arvind Panagariya was NITI's first Vice-Chairperson (2015-17) and later chaired the 16th Finance Commission.

s: Who served as CEO of NITI Aayog from February 2023 to February 2026?
x: B.V.R. Subrahmanyam was CEO from 25 February 2023 to 24 February 2026; Anurag Jain was appointed in July 2026.

s: Who succeeded Rajiv Kumar as Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in May 2022?
x: Suman K. Bery was Vice-Chairperson from May 2022 to April 2026, after Rajiv Kumar (2017-22).

s: Before becoming Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in April 2026, Ashok Kumar Lahiri had served as which of the following?
x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri, an economist and West Bengal MLA, is a former Chief Economic Adviser.

s: Which Director General of the DMEO served as interim CEO of NITI Aayog?
x: Nidhi Chhibber, DG of DMEO, was interim CEO between regular CEOs.

s: Which of the following is one of the four principal areas of NITI Aayog's mandate?
x: NITI Aayog's mandate covers knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, driving transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of NITI Aayog in its Cabinet resolution?
o: Ensuring national security interests are considered in economic policy
Allocating plan funds and grants to the States
x: NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power; allocating plan funds was the Planning Commission's role.

s: Which of the following is NOT a guiding priority of NITI Aayog?
x: An exclusive preference for large enterprises is contrary to NITI Aayog's approach, which includes Antyodaya, small enterprises and inclusive development.

s: State rankings issued by NITI Aayog are primarily associated with which form of federal competition?
x: NITI Aayog’s State rankings encourage competitive federalism by comparing performance across States and promoting improvement.

s: NITI Aayog's core approach combines cooperative federalism with which approach?
x: NITI Aayog combines cooperative federalism with a bottom-up approach, giving States a bigger say in policy.

s: Under NITI Aayog's Cabinet resolution, credible plans are to be formulated at which level and aggregated progressively upwards?
x: The resolution calls for credible plans at village level, aggregated progressively to higher levels.

s:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog's guiding approach:
1. It follows a bottom-up approach.
2. It embraces Antyodaya.
3. It gives sole preference to large enterprises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NITI's approach is bottom-up, cooperative federalism and Antyodaya, with a focus on small enterprises; it does not prefer only large enterprises.

s: What is competition among sub-national units such as States and cities on governance indicators called?
x: Competitive sub-federalism means competition among States, cities and other sub-national units on governance indicators.

s: Which term is used for the cooperative federalism that NITI Aayog follows?
x: NITI's guiding approach is cooperative, or 'marble-cake', federalism.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of NITI Aayog?
o: The resolution fixes the number of full-time members at five.
The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister.
The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
Up to two part-time members may come from universities and research institutions.
x: The resolution does not prescribe a fixed number of full-time members; the other three statements are correct.

s: Which NITI Aayog office-holder has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India?
x: The CEO, appointed by the Prime Minister, has a fixed tenure and the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

s: What is the maximum number of part-time members of NITI Aayog?
x: NITI Aayog can have at most 2 part-time members, from universities and research bodies, on a rotational basis.

s: At most how many Union Ministers can the Prime Minister nominate as ex-officio members of NITI Aayog?
x: Up to 4 Union Ministers nominated by the PM are ex-officio members.

s: Who appoints the Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
x: The Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister and holds Cabinet Minister rank.

s: What rank does the Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog hold?
o: Secretary to the Government of India
x: The Vice-Chairperson has Cabinet Minister rank; the CEO holds the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

s: Who are the special invitees of NITI Aayog?
o: Chief Ministers nominated by the President
Domain experts and practitioners nominated by the PM
x: Special invitees are domain experts and practitioners nominated by the Prime Minister.

s: What is the number of full-time members of NITI Aayog?
x:
'five at present' – now seven full-time members (June 2026, Praveen CA360).
The number of full-time members is not fixed – three in 2015, five in most books, seven since June 2026. Up to eight full-time members was the Planning Commission's limit.

s: Which former Cabinet Secretary became a full-time member of NITI Aayog in the reconstituted panel of 2026?
x: Rajiv Gauba, former Cabinet Secretary, is a full-time member in the panel reconstituted in April 2026.

s: How many full-time members did NITI Aayog have when it was set up in 2015?
x: The 2015 set-up had 3 full-time members; the number is not fixed and is 5 at present.

s: Who among the following was reported in June 2026 as a new full-time member of NITI Aayog?
x: Joram Aniya and R. Balasubramaniam were reported as new full-time members in June 2026.

s: The Governing Council of NITI Aayog has taken over the work of which body?
x: The Governing Council has taken over the work earlier associated with the National Development Council.

s: In the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, who represents Union Territories with legislatures such as Delhi and Puducherry?
x: UTs with legislatures, such as Delhi and Puducherry, are represented by their Chief Ministers; only the other UTs send Lieutenant Governors.

s: Who convenes the Regional Councils of NITI Aayog?
x: Regional Councils, dealing with issues affecting more than one State, are convened by the Prime Minister.

s: On which date was the 11th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog held?
x: The Governing Council usually meets once a year; its 11th meeting was held on 11 June 2026.

s: What was the theme of the 11th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, held on 11 June 2026?
o: Innovation and Growth for Atmanirbhar Bharat
Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047
x: The 11th Governing Council meeting was held under the theme “Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047”.

s: Who jointly head the Regional Councils of NITI Aayog?
o: A rotational Chief Minister of the group and a Central Minister
The Prime Minister and the Vice-Chairperson
The Union Home Minister and the Governors
The CEO and the Chief Secretaries
x: Regional Councils deal with issues affecting more than one State and are headed jointly by a rotational CM and a Central Minister.

s: How many Chief Ministers attended the 11th Governing Council meeting of NITI Aayog, the first with 100% attendance?
x: The 11th meeting on 11 June 2026 was the first attended by all 28 Chief Ministers.

s: When was the Governing Council of NITI Aayog first constituted?
x: It was first constituted in February 2015 and reconstituted in February 2021.

s: Who headed the committee of Chief Ministers on digital payments set up under NITI Aayog in 2016?
x: After the 2015 sub-groups of CMs, a CMs' committee on digital payments (2016) was set up under Chandrababu Naidu.

s: What was the theme of the 10th meeting of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog held in 2025?
o: Inclusive Human Development for Viksit Bharat@2047
x: The 10th meeting (2025) had the theme 'Viksit Rajya for Viksit Bharat@2047'; the 11th (2026) was on inclusive human development.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the sub-groups of Chief Ministers formed by NITI Aayog in 2015?
x: The 2015 CM sub-groups were on centrally sponsored schemes, skill development and Swachh Bharat.

s: The DMEO was formed in 2015 by merging the Programme Evaluation Organisation (PEO) with which body?
x: DMEO was formed by merging the PEO and the IEO; NILERD (formerly IAMR) is a separate autonomous institute.

s: Who chairs the SETU (State Economic and Transformation Units) Steering Committee of NITI Aayog?
x: The SETU Steering Committee is chaired by the CEO of NITI Aayog, not the Vice-Chairperson.

s: What is the full form of DMEO?
x: DMEO is the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office, attached to NITI Aayog.

s: What does AIM 2.0 primarily seek to do?
o: Fill ecosystem gaps and scale innovations
x: AIM 2.0 is intended to fill gaps in the innovation ecosystem and scale up innovations.

s: What is NILERD, associated with NITI Aayog?
o: An attached office formed by merging PEO and IEO
A regional council chaired by the Prime Minister
An autonomous institute formerly known as IAMR
x: NILERD is an autonomous institute under NITI Aayog and was formerly known as the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR).

s: Which two hubs function within NITI Aayog?
o: Team India Hub and Fund Allocation Hub
Team India Hub and Knowledge and Innovation Hub
State Finance Hub and Knowledge and Innovation Hub
x: NITI's two hubs are the Team India Hub (Centre-State partnership) and the Knowledge and Innovation Hub.

s: AIM 2.0 was approved in 2024 with an outlay of Rs 2,750 crore. Up to when does it run?
x: AIM 2.0 (2024) has Rs 2,750 crore up to March 2028.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SETU Steering Committee – chaired by the Vice-Chairperson
Atal Innovation Mission – set up in 2018
DMEO – merger of PEO and IEO
x: DMEO (2015) merged the PEO and IEO. NILERD was formerly IAMR, the SETU committee is chaired by the CEO and AIM began in 2016.

s: Which body was set up on 18 September 2015 as an attached office of NITI Aayog?
x: The DMEO, formed by merging PEO and IEO, was set up on 18 September 2015 as an attached office of NITI Aayog.

s: In which year was the Atal Innovation Mission, the flagship initiative of NITI Aayog, launched?
x: The Atal Innovation Mission was launched in 2016; AIM 2.0 followed in 2024.

s: Under NITI Aayog's State Support Mission, what is Maharashtra's state transformation unit called?
x: States set up SETUs to draft State Vision@2047: Maharashtra's is MITRA and Assam's is SITA.

s: Which of the following programmes is run by NITI Aayog?
x: NITI Aayog runs the Aspirational Districts Programme and the SDG India Index.

s: Under NITI Aayog's State Support Mission, what is Assam's state transformation unit called?
x: Assam's unit is SITA and Maharashtra's is MITRA.

s: Swarna Andhra @2047, aligned with Viksit Bharat @2047, was written under which NITI Aayog initiative?
x: State Vision @2047 documents such as Swarna Andhra @2047 are written by States under the State Support Mission.

s: The first Three-Year Action Agenda of NITI Aayog covered which period?
x: The first Three-Year Action Agenda covered the period from 2017–18 to 2019–20.

s: Which period did NITI Aayog's 7-year Strategy cover?
x: The 7-year Strategy ran from 2017-18 to 2023-24; the Three Year Action Agenda covered 2017-18 to 2019-20.

s: Who launched NITI Aayog's 'Strategy for New India @75', released on 19 December 2018?
x: Strategy for New India @75 was launched by Arun Jaitley on 19 December 2018.

s: Up to which year does NITI Aayog's 15-year Vision document run?
x: The 15-year Vision runs up to 2030, alongside the 7-year Strategy and 3-year Action Agenda mandated in 2016.

s: How many areas does the 'Strategy for New India @75' cover?
x: Strategy for New India @75 covers 41 areas with targets for 2022-23.

s: Through what was the Planning Commission set up on 15 March 1950, and who was its first chairman?
o: an Act of Parliament; Jawaharlal Nehru
x: Like NITI Aayog later (1 January 2015), the Planning Commission was created by a Cabinet resolution on 15 March 1950, with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru as its first chairman. It was never statutory (no Act) or constitutional, and neither Patel nor Rajendra Prasad chaired it.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Planning Commission was an advisory body.
The Planning Commission was a constitutional body.
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission.
The Finance Commission is constituted periodically.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Planning Commission was a non-constitutional, non-statutory advisory body created by a Cabinet resolution in 1950. NITI Aayog replaced it, and the Finance Commission is set up every five years.

s: To which posts in NITI Aayog do the Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary of the Planning Commission correspond?
x: The Planning Commission had a Deputy Chairman and Member-Secretary; NITI Aayog has a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO.

s: In 2016, which set of documents was NITI Aayog asked by the Prime Minister’s Office to prepare in place of the Five-Year Plans?
o: Twenty-Year Vision, Ten-Year Strategy and Two-Year Action Plan
Fifteen-Year Vision, Five-Year Strategy and Seven-Year Action Agenda
Fifteen-Year Vision, Seven-Year Strategy and Three-Year Action Agenda
Ten-Year Vision, Five-Year Strategy and Annual Action Plan
x: In 2016, NITI Aayog was asked to prepare a Fifteen-Year Vision, a Seven-Year Strategy and a Three-Year Action Agenda to replace the Five-Year Plans.

s: Which body allocated plan funds and grants to the States?
x: The Planning Commission allocated plan funds and grants; NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power and is advisory.

s: The Planning Commission could have up to how many full-time members?
x: The Planning Commission had up to eight full-time members and no part-time members.

s: With reference to the role of States, which statement is correct?
o: NITI Aayog restricts States to annual plan talks.
Under the Planning Commission every Chief Minister was a permanent member of its Governing Council.
Under NITI Aayog every Chief Minister sits on the Governing Council, giving States a direct role.
The Planning Commission gave States a direct role through its Governing Council.
x: The Planning Commission limited the role of States largely to the National Development Council and annual plan discussions, whereas NITI Aayog gives every Chief Minister a direct role through its Governing Council.

s: The Planning Commission, unlike NITI Aayog, followed which approach to planning?
x: The Planning Commission's plans were top-down and one-size-fits-all; NITI is bottom-up with a Vision-Strategy-Action Agenda.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Planning Commission:
1. It had no part-time members.
